channels.name: SCLK
channels.purpose: Serial clock (SDR one edge, DDR both edges).

channels.name: CS#
channels.purpose: Active-low chip select; frames each command.

channels.name: IO0..IO3 (Quad) / IO0..IO7 (Octal)
channels.purpose: Multi-IO data (instruction/address/data per phase). IO0=MOSI, IO1=MISO single; /WP->IO2, /HOLD->IO3 in Quad.

handshake_pairs.name: CS# / command frame
handshake_pairs.rule: CS# low begins, CS# high ends each command.

handshake_pairs.name: instruction / phase select
handshake_pairs.rule: Opcode selects the address/mode/dummy/data phase sequence and lane counts.

handshake_pairs.name: dummy cycles / read latency
handshake_pairs.rule: Dummy cycles must equal the device read latency for the mode/frequency.

handshake_pairs.name: DQS / read data
handshake_pairs.rule: Octal DDR: DQS edge-aligned to read data on IO0..IO7.

handshake_pairs.name: WEL/WIP / program-erase
handshake_pairs.rule: WREN sets WEL; controller polls WIP via 0x05 for completion.

dependency_graph.common_rule: Every command is framed by CS#; phases run in order instruction -> address -> [mode] -> dummy -> data, each on 1/2/4/8 lanes, MSB-first. DQS (octal DDR) accompanies read data. The opcode determines which phases are present.
dependency_graph.data_dependency: A correct read requires (1) the right protocol mode / lane count for the opcode, (2) the right address-byte count (3 vs 4), and (3) the right dummy-cycle count for the frequency. A program/erase requires WEL set (0x06) first and WIP polling for completion.

ordering_rules.phase_order: instruction, address, mode bits, dummy cycles, data.
ordering_rules.transaction_atomicity: One command per CS# assertion; point-to-point per chip-select.
